newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Former Botswana bourse head gets jail sentence.
newsitem.headline: Former Botswana bourse head gets jail sentence.

text.p: A former chairman of the Botswana Stock Exchange (BSE) was sentenced on Tuesday to three years imprisonment on corruption charges, two of them suspended.

John Stoneham, 48, has held a host of high-profile positions including manager of the Botswana Motor Vehicle Insurance Fund, and acting permanent secretary in the Ministry of Finance and chairman of the BSE.
Stoneham is expected to appeal against his sentencing by a magistrate's court. He had pleaded guilty to fraud during his management of the Motor Vehicle Insurance Fund.
Stoneham was largely responsible for getting the BSE off the ground in 1995, and chaired the steering committee to change the former Botswana Share Market to a fully fledged exchange.
He was appointed first chairman of the BSE, but the appointment was not renewed when it expired in October 1996.
